observations.rule: HttpOnly excludes cookie exposure to non-HTTP APIs but does not disable HTTP request cookie attachment; Secure controls transport.

optionAudit.blocks-fetch: Overstates HttpOnly as a request prohibition
optionAudit.limited-boundary: Separates script reads from browser request attachment
optionAudit.secure-encryption: Secure does not implement this claimed script isolation

observations.rule: PHP upload documentation identifies the type field as client-supplied and not checked by PHP; server content inspection addresses a separate validation requirement.

optionAudit.inspect-bytes: Uses the required server-side byte evidence

observations.expectedError: must not be accessed before initialization

observations.rule: The stated domain API must express only the shared validation decision. Each entry point owns the required HTTP status or CLI exit code; adding a transport must not alter the domain API.

optionAudit.http-domain: HTTP status 422 becomes part of the shared API, making the CLI depend on HTTP semantics.
optionAudit.sapi-branch: Transport detection and per-transport branches move into the shared validation service.
optionAudit.domain-outcome: A neutral validation result is reusable; the entry points separately map it to 422 or 2.
optionAudit.paired-statuses: The domain result carries transport-specific fields and needs extension for another transport.

observations.rule: Composer files autoloading includes declared files on autoloader inclusion; autoload-dev is root-only.

optionAudit.files: Includes the required declaration before the first function call.
optionAudit.psr4: No class lookup occurs at the function call.
optionAudit.classmap: Does not make standalone function calls trigger loading.
optionAudit.dev-files: A dependency cannot export its required API through its own root-only development configuration.

observations.rule: $_REQUEST contents and ordering depend on request_order/variables_order; a body-only form contract must use the body source.

optionAudit.request: Cannot guarantee provenance across configuration changes.
optionAudit.merge: Admits query-only action when the body omits it.
optionAudit.fallback: Admits an alternate source precisely when the body field is missing.
optionAudit.post: Keeps body presence and scalar validation explicit.

observations.rule: Apply the explicit mutex and visibility assumptions to the stated two-worker schedule.

optionAudit.recheck: B reads the newly published value under the lock.
optionAudit.skip-wait: A waiting contender can return null instead of a value.

observations.rule: Evaluate each design against both early failure and two simultaneous instance values.

optionAudit.method-env: Fails the pre-order validation and independent-instance requirements.
optionAudit.static-cache: Fails early validation and shares one value.
optionAudit.constructor-value: Meets both requirements through explicit validated construction.
optionAudit.global-constant: Meets early validation but cannot represent two instance values.

observations.rule: Use the stated monotonic token and atomic storage comparison contract; no real distributed service is contacted.

optionAudit.long-lease: A longer finite pause still defeats the timing assumption.
optionAudit.local-check: A pause after the check preserves the race.
optionAudit.unlock-check: The check occurs after the harmful mutation.

observations.rule: Evaluate the provided 6-before-5 schedule with atomic applied-version updates and durable gap recovery.

optionAudit.id-only: Applies a distinct but premature version 6.
optionAudit.recover-gap: Preserves order and retains a route to eventual application.

observations.rule: PostgreSQL SET LOCAL lasts only for the current transaction; apply the explicit connection lifecycle and fail-closed policy premises.

optionAudit.session-once: Leaks connection-lifetime identity into later tenants.
optionAudit.local-every-job: Context expires with each successfully ended transaction.
optionAudit.after-success: The session SET occurs before BEGIN, so rollback does not undo it and failure skips cleanup.
